newsitem.title: USA: Alltel, Integrated Healthcare set venture.
newsitem.headline: Alltel, Integrated Healthcare set venture.

text.p: Alltel Corp and Integrated Healthcare Solutions Inc said Friday they have formed a new company that will combine their resources in offering healthcare information technology and services worldwide.

Called Eclipsys Corp, the new company will combine the healthcare information services unit of Alltel, which is based in Little Rock, Ark., and Integrated Healthcare Solutions, a privately held company based here.
Eclipsys will be privately held, with 15 percent of its capital held by Alltel, according to Integrated Healthcare, spokeswoman Stephanie Massengil.
In the transaction, Alltel will receive $154 million in cash and preferred stock convertible into the 15 percent stake, she said.

The remaining 85 percent will be held by founding members of Integrated Healthcare Solutions, including teaching affiliates of the Harvard Medical School, a group of strategic investors and a team of healthcare information technology executives, she said.
The combination will be treated as a pooling of interests and will be financed by a group led by General Atlantic Partners, a private investment firm, she said.

As part of the transaction, General Atlantic, First Union Capital Partners, a unit of First Union Corp, and BT Capital Partners, a unit of Bankers Trust New York Corp will invest $100 million in Integrated Healthcare Solutions, she said.
In addition, First Union National Bank of North Carolina will extend a $30 million debt financing, she said.

"The unique combination ... of the two companies and their products and services represents the next generation of health information technology, said Harvey Wilson, chairman and chief executive officer of Eclipsys and former head of Integrated Healthcare Solutions.

Alltel, an information technology company that has investments in wired and wireless communications services, will have one board member in Eclipsys and will supply the new company with various services under a four-year agreement, according to an announcement by both companies.
Eclipsys will have 1,000 employees and will have offices in Atlanta; Boston; Malvern, Pa.; Roseland, N.J.; San Jose, Calif.;, and several European locations, the announcement said.
